paragraphs.text: Lesson 29, ready for an adventure?
Steve's trying to convince his friend Andy to go rock climbing with him.
Listen to their conversation and answer these eight comprehension questions.
Any chance you'd be up for some rock climbing this weekend?
Eh, rock climbing isn't really my thing. I'm more of a basketball guy.
Exactly. You're tall. You've got good reach.
So you'd probably be a natural at rock climbing.
Okay, I'll hear me you. What have you got in mind?
There's an indoor gym just 20 minutes from here.
They've got a whole bunch of walls, some for beginners, some for hardcore climbers.
You just have to do a half hour training session to learn how to use the harness and stuff,
and then they turn you loose on the walls.
Hmm, on second thought I got a couple of things to take care of this weekend.
Don't chicken out on me? Listen, they're always hosting kids' birthday parties there.
If eight-year-old girls can do it, so can you.
Man, just thinking about being 50 feet up with nothing but a flimsy harness?
It's making my hands sweaty.
You don't strike me as the type to be afraid of heights.
Haven't you done any extreme sports before?
Uh, what qualifies as an extreme sport?
You know, anything that makes adrenaline rush through your veins.
White water rafting, jet skiing, skydiving, or bungee jumping.
That sort of thing.
My family needs to ski. Does that count?
Depends. Were you like weaving in and out of trees or were you on the bunny trail?
We definitely stayed on the easier slopes.
I just don't get white so exciting to put your life at risk.
You know, statistically, your life's more at risk when you're behind the wheel than when you're skiing or rock climbing.
Heck, either of us could drop dead of a heart attack in the next five minutes.
Nobody's invincible.
Okay, I'll give you that.
But I don't see why I should increase my chances by flirting with death.
It's hard to explain.
I just love the nervous anticipation leading up to it.
Will I be able to pull it off?
And then when you're finally doing it, you get that surge of energy.
And afterwards, you feel like you could take on the world.
It's hard to disagree when you get all fired up like that.
But I'm a pretty big guy.
Are you sure those ropes can hold me?
What if they snap?
Well, just in case the floor is padded.
But trust me, the ropes won't snap.
They've been tested with over 500 pounds.
Climbing gyms have to meet all sorts of safety standards in order to operate.
Alright, I guess I'll give it a shot.
But next weekend, let's do something tamer like playing tennis.
Yeah, so you can kick my butt on the court to get back at me for making you try rock climbing.
I haven't played tennis in years.
I'm really rusty.
Hey, I gotta pick up my brother's kids from daycare.
Where's this rock climbing gym anyway?
I'll text you the address.
Cool.
Catch you later.
Alright, now let's learn the vocabulary.
Steve asks, any chance you'd be up for some rock climbing this weekend?
This expression, you'd be up for, means you would want to.
If you say you're up for something, it means you want to do it.
And if you say you're not up for something, it means you really don't want to do it at
that moment.
And he replies that rock climbing isn't really his thing.
He's more of a basketball guy.
And Steve argues that because Andy is tall, he'd probably be a natural at rock climbing.
A natural is someone who has natural ability and learns quickly.
Then Andy says, okay, I'll humor you.
To humor someone means to go along with what they want, to comply or agree with them, in order
to make that person happy.
He asks Steve, what have you got in mind?
What have you got in mind means what are you thinking about?
Steve describes an indoor rock climbing gym, which has walls for both beginners and hardcore
climbers.
A hardcore climber is someone who does rock climbing intensely, who likes difficulty and
challenges.
Steve explains that you have to do a half hour training session to learn how to use the harness.
A harness is a piece of safety equipment.
It consists of straps that will hold your body up in case you fall.
After the training session, they turn you loose on the walls.
Turn you loose means they let you go freely.
Andy says, hmm, on second thought, I've got a couple of things to take care of this weekend.
You can say, on second thought, when you're reconsidering something that you said earlier.
Steve replies, don't chicken out on me.
To chicken out means to become scared and not do something.
Steve says the rock climbing gym is always hosting kids birthday parties.
To host means to have someone or something at your place.
But Andy doesn't like to think about being 50 feet up with nothing but a flimsy harness.
The word flimsy means weak and fragile and might break easily.
Steve replies, you don't strike me as the type to be afraid of heights.
You don't strike me as means you don't seem like.
Steve asks Andy if he's ever done extreme sports and then Steve gives some examples,
like whitewater rafting.
That's going on an inflatable boat in rivers with very agitated water.
Jet skiing is going on the ocean on a fast, motorized individual boat.
Skydiving, meaning jumping out of an airplane with a parachute.
And bungee jumping, meaning jumping off a bridge or high place with an elastic cord tied to
your legs.
Andy says his family used to ski, but Steve asks if he was weaving in and out of trees or
if he was on the bunny trail.
To weave in and out of the trees means to go around the trees to one side of each tree
and then to the other side.
It would be quite dangerous to ski while weaving in and out of trees.
Or Steve says where you are on the bunny trail.
The bunny trail is the least dangerous hill in a ski resort.
The bunny trail is designed for children and beginner skiers.
Andy definitely stayed on the easier slopes.
The word slopes means hills.
Andy says I just don't get why it's so exciting to put your life at risk.
I don't get is a slang way to say I don't understand.
Steve argues that statistically your life's more at risk when you're behind the wheel than
when you're skiing or rock climbing.
Behind the wheel means driving.
Steve points out that nobody's invincible.
Invincible means unable to be hurt or unable to be defeated.
Andy says okay, I'll give you that.
I'll give you that means I'll admit that your point is correct.
But Andy still doesn't see why he should increase his chances by flirting with death.
Flirting with death means doing dangerous things where you might be killed.
Steve loves the nervous anticipation leading up to an extreme sport.
Leading up to means coming before.
He wonders will I be able to pull it off?
To pull it off means to manage to do something difficult.
Then when you're finally doing the activity, Steve says you get a surge of energy.
A surge is a sudden increase.
And afterwards you feel like you can take on the world.
You can take on the world means you can do anything.
You can face and defeat any challenge.
Andy says it's hard to disagree when you get all fired up like that.
Fired up means full of intense emotion.
But Andy is still nervous about the ropes at the climbing gym.
He asks what if they snap?
Snap means to break.
Just in case the floor of the gym is padded says Steve.
Padded means covered in soft material that will protect you on impact.
Andy says he'll give it a shot.
Give it a shot means try it.
But next weekend he'd prefer to do something tamer like playing tennis.
Tamer means less crazy or less dangerous.
Steve replies, yeah, so you can kick my butt on the court.
To kick someone's butt is a slang way to talk about beating someone at a game or competition
or physically beating them up.
In this case, Steve says that Andy can kick his butt, meaning that Andy can beat him at tennis.
Andy can win all the tennis games.
Steve thinks Andy wants to play tennis in order to get back at him for the rock climbing.
To get back at someone means to get revenge on that person.
Steve hasn't played tennis in years and he's really rusty.
If you're rusty it means you perform badly because you haven't practiced in a long time.
You're out of practice.
Andy has to leave because he has to go pick up his brothers' kids from daycare.
Daycare is a place where children are taken care of during the day.
Children in daycare are usually not yet old enough to go to school, but their parents work,
so they go to a daycare center in order to be taken care of in the daytime.
Steve says he'll text Andy the address, and Andy replies, cool, catch you later.
Catch you later is an informal way to say see you later.
That's all the vocabulary from today's conversation.
Go ahead and try the vocabulary quiz to put these expressions into practice and the speaking
task to get some feedback on your spoken English.
